question.problem:
A particle of mass $0.8\,\text{kg}$ is attached to a massless spring. An external periodic force 

$$
F(t)=(4{cos}^{2}\,(\frac{5}{2}t)-2)\,\text{N}
$$

is applied to the particle.

The position of the particle is $y(t)$ (measured in meters), and $t>0$ is the time in seconds. If the particle moves with forced harmonic motion without damping and the system experiences resonance, what is the spring constant $k?$

$k=$
{{field-1}}${\text{kg/s}}^{2}$
question.worked_solution:
The equation of motion for a particle of mass $m$ moving with forced harmonic motion without damping under the action of a spring with spring constant $k$ and external force $F(t)$ is given by

$$
m{y}^{″}=-ky+F(t).
$$

Substituting our values for $m$ and $F(t)$ gives

$$
0.8{y}^{″}=-ky+(4{cos}^{2}\,(\frac{5}{2}t)-2).
$$

Simplifying and rearranging the above equation, we get

$$
{y}^{″}+\frac{5k}{4}y=\frac{5}{2}(2{cos}^{2}\,(\frac{5}{2}t)-1).
$$

The complementary solution ${y}_{c}$ here represents simple harmonic motion, and it can be written as

$$
{y}_{c}=A\operatorname{cos}⁡\omega t+B\operatorname{sin}⁡\omega t,
$$

where $A$ and $B$ are arbitrary constants of integration, and $\omega $ is the system's internal frequency.

In our case,

$$
{\omega }^{2}=\frac{5k}{4}\,⟹\,k=\frac{4}{5}{\omega }^{2}.
$$

The oscillator experiences resonance when the frequency of the external periodic force $f(t)=\frac{5}{2}(2{cos}^{2}\,(\frac{5}{2}t)-1)$ is equal to the frequency of the complementary solution $\omega .$ Since

$$
f(t)=\frac{5}{2}(2{cos}^{2}\,(\frac{5}{2}t)-1)=\frac{5}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t),
$$

the frequency of the external periodic force is $5.$

Therefore,

$$
k=\frac{4}{5}{\omega }^{2}=\frac{4}{5}\cdot {5}^{2}=20\,{\text{kg/s}}^{2}.
$$
